runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Persisted sessions in disposable HOME and CODEX_HOME; generated Skill under .agents/skills and generated evidence_reader definition under .codex/agents; repeated with and without --ignore-user-config.
runtime.permissionProfile: Read-only sandbox with approval policy never

assertions.evidence: The parent loaded the generated check-custom-role Skill in both runs.
The parent located and read .codex/agents/evidence-reader.toml, including its name, sandbox, and developer instructions.
The available spawn_agent tool schema had no role or agent-type selector, so the parent could not select evidence_reader.
No worker was started because the Skill forbids substituting a general-purpose worker for the generated role.
Both external post-run git status checks were clean.

limitations: This is a surface- and version-specific negative observation. Official documentation describes custom agents, but Codex CLI 0.155.1 did not expose a role selector in the actual spawn tool used by codex exec.
The probe was repeated without --ignore-user-config to rule out that flag as the cause.
A later runtime version or another Codex surface may expose the documented custom-agent selection mechanism and requires a separate probe.
